structured_output.scope_summary: EIP-7935, at this revision, is an Informational EIP. It asks execution-layer clients to raise the gas limit in their default configurations from the current 36M on mainnet to a target of 'XX0M' by the Fusaka release. The Security Considerations section names 60M as the value to test. It adds no consensus rule, transaction type, opcode, header field or encoding change. The specification only asks clients to update their default configuration values. The required work is mostly performance and safety validation: devnets running all EL/CL client combinations with full synthetic blocks, a check of worst-case block size against the 10 MiB CL gossip limit, and coordinated scheduling with a separately proposed 30M transaction gas limit cap.

evidence.locator: Specification — "update the gas limit value generated in their default configurations"
evidence.summary: Only the default configuration value changes. No gas charging, metering or consensus limit rule changes.

evm_gas_rule_changes.rationale: The block gas limit is still set by validators under the unchanged adjustment rule. Changing a client's default target does not change any execution-gas accounting rule or parameter in consensus.
evm_gas_rule_changes.uncertainty_note: One could argue that the effective block gas limit is a 'limit'. However, the EIP changes defaults, not a consensus parameter.

evidence.summary: No change to how instructions access state or charge gas.

state_access_ordering_within_opcode_exec.rationale: No instruction ordering is changed or introduced.

evidence.summary: Only the execution gas limit default is mentioned. Blob gas is not mentioned.
No state-gas accounting is defined or changed.
No refund mechanism is mentioned.

evidence.locator: Backwards Compatibility — "A higher gas limit should not break any existing contracts"
evidence.summary: No behavioral change is described for existing execution.

patterns_affecting_pre_existing_tests.rationale: Consensus tests set their own environment or genesis gas limits. A change to client defaults does not require reworking baseline test inputs or expected results.
patterns_affecting_pre_existing_tests.uncertainty_note: No test suite was supplied. Any test that relied on a client default instead of an explicit gas limit would be a local issue.

evidence.summary: No new output, field or commitment is introduced.

new_invariant_on_pre_existing_tests.rationale: No new assertion is needed in baseline tests.

evidence.summary: Only client default configurations change. The t8n tool already takes the gas limit as an input.

transition_tool_interface_changes.rationale: No transition-tool field or mechanism change is required.

evidence.locator: Security Considerations — "Synthetic transactions will be created until blocks are full"
evidence.summary: The validation uses full synthetic blocks on devnets, not new consensus test abstractions.

new_test_framework_primitives.rationale: The block gas limit is already a parameter of existing test construction. No new primitive is architecturally required for EL consensus tests.
new_test_framework_primitives.uncertainty_note: Performance or benchmark tooling for filling 60M blocks may need local extensions. This is not established by the supplied text.

evidence.summary: No cryptographic content.
Changes a default value only. The gas limit adjustment and validation rules are unchanged.

edge_boundary_conditions.rationale: No consensus rule with boundary-sensitive outcomes is introduced or changed. The new default target is a parameter value, not a new rule.
edge_boundary_conditions.uncertainty_note: Block-full boundary cases at 60M are useful for performance work but are not a changed consensus boundary.

evidence.summary: No change to block decoding or structural validation.

block_syncing_changes.rationale: The gas limit header validation rules are unchanged.

evidence.summary: No Engine API change is mentioned.

engine_api_changes.rationale: No Engine API fields or endpoints change.

evidence.summary: No system contracts are introduced.
No system contract is referenced.
No opcodes are introduced.
No opcode semantics change. The GASLIMIT opcode's semantics are unchanged; only its observed value may differ.

modified_opcodes.rationale: No instruction semantics or availability change.

evidence.summary: No precompiles are introduced.
No precompile changes.
No schema or codec changes.
No new transaction envelope.

evidence.locator: Backwards Compatibility — "new transactions could exceed the proposed 30M transaction gas limit"
evidence.summary: The transaction gas cap is defined by a different proposal. This EIP does not change any validity rule.

new_or_modified_transaction_validity_mec.rationale: No consensus transaction-validity or intrinsic-gas rule is changed by this EIP. A larger block gas limit only lets bigger transactions fit under the unchanged block gas limit check.

evidence.summary: No header fields are added.

evidence.locator: Rationale — "tying a new value to a hard fork release"
evidence.summary: The fork is only a coordination point for releasing new defaults. It involves no state transition.

evidence.locator: Security Considerations — "the gas limit will be increased incrementally"
evidence.summary: The increase happens gradually through the existing gas limit voting, not through an activation transition.

new_fork_activation_mechanism.rationale: No activation-specific EL state transition is required.

evidence.locator: Security Considerations — "Devnets will be stood up with nodes running all combinations of EL and CL clients in order to test if a gas limit of 60M is safe"
evidence.summary: Requires integrated stress testing across all client combinations at the higher limit.

evidence.locator: Security Considerations — "Synthetic transactions will be created until blocks are full, and network and node health monitored"
evidence.summary: Full-block workloads at 60M must be validated for block execution, node health and networking.

evidence.locator: Security Considerations — "current worst-case block size of 1.79 MiB would reach the current 10MiB CL gossip limit"
evidence.summary: Adversarial block-size constructions couple the execution gas limit with the CL gossip size bound.

evidence.locator: Motivation — "we expect to find bugs in clients at higher gas limits"
evidence.summary: Higher execution capacity is expected to expose new client performance issues.

performance_risks.rationale: Raising the default gas limit from 36M to about 60M raises the resource bound for every existing workload. The affected assumptions are worst-case block execution and validation time within a slot, state and IO load, and block size versus the 10 MiB CL gossip limit. The EIP itself requires adversarial and full-block stress testing across EL/CL client combinations and networking. This meets level 3: adversarial workload combinations need integrated stress testing across distinct execution and client subsystems.
performance_risks.uncertainty_note: The EIP changes only defaults, not consensus rules. It also says the block-size coupling should not matter below 150M, which could argue for level 2 (bounded interaction).

evidence.locator: Security Considerations — "Adversarial block constructions that would increase the worst-case size ... should not be a factor below 150M gas"
evidence.summary: The increase changes the DoS bound on worst-case block size and execution, which interacts with the CL gossip size limit.

evidence.locator: Security Considerations — "If bugs are discovered, client teams will patch them"
evidence.summary: Validating safety at the new limit is part of the planned process.

security_risks.rationale: The larger gas limit changes the worst-case resource bound that other components rely on. These include CL gossip message size and node liveness under maximally expensive blocks. This is a bounded interaction that needs targeted adversarial integration review. It does not change shared authorization or trust invariants.
security_risks.uncertainty_note: A safety analysis limited to DoS could be seen as overlapping with PERF. Level 1 is possible if the gossip-limit margin is accepted as already researched.

evidence.locator: Specification — "Execution layer clients have different configuration formats"
evidence.summary: Defaults are client configuration, not a consensus outcome.

unspecified_behavior_requiring_cross_cli.rationale: The value placeholder and the incremental increase schedule are open. However, client default configuration is not a consensus-visible protocol outcome, so no unresolved consensus outcome is identified.
unspecified_behavior_requiring_cross_cli.uncertainty_note: The XX0M/60M inconsistency is a real gap in the document, but it affects planning and validation targets, not consensus results.

evidence.locator: Backwards Compatibility — "new transactions could exceed the proposed 30M transaction gas limit, so the scheduling of these two EIPs should be coordinated"
evidence.summary: Interacts with a separately proposed per-transaction gas cap. That EIP's number is not given and it is not in the candidate list.

cross_eip_interactions.rationale: The only stated interaction is with the proposed 30M per-transaction gas limit. Testing needs only local compatibility checks: blocks with a 60M limit holding transactions near or above 30M, with the cap active or inactive. Otherwise the target can be tested independently.
cross_eip_interactions.uncertainty_note: The cap EIP's text is not supplied. Its exact semantics, and whether it is scheduled in the same fork, are evidence gaps.

unidentified_interactions: A proposed 30M per-transaction gas limit cap (EIP number not given in the supplied text). The two EIPs need coordinated scheduling. Local compatibility cases: blocks at a 60M limit containing transactions above 30M, with the cap active or inactive.

under_specification.summary: The recommended gas limit is still a placeholder ('XX0M') in the title, abstract and specification. Security Considerations names 60M as the value to test. The schedule for the incremental increase and the conditions for moving from the 36M baseline are not specified. None of this is consensus-visible, but it sets how large the performance and security validation target is.
unresolved_questions: What is the final recommended default gas limit: 60M or another 'XX0M' value?
What is the incremental increase schedule, and what are the go/no-go criteria for each step?
Which EIP defines the 30M transaction gas cap, and is it scheduled for the same fork?

notable_ambiguities: The title, abstract and specification say 'XX0M' (a TODO placeholder), while Security Considerations tests 60M.
The EIP is Informational and changes client defaults rather than consensus rules, yet it asks to be included in a hard fork as a commitment.
It does not say whether the 10 MiB gossip limit or the 1.79 MiB worst-case block size will be re-checked at the final value.
